easy.explanation: The Lord addresses Jacob, His servant, and Israel, whom He has chosen.
easy.q: To whom does the Lord speak at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: The Lord says He will pour water upon the thirsty and floods upon the dry ground.
easy.q: What does the Lord promise to pour upon the thirsty and dry ground?

easy.explanation: He promises to pour His spirit upon the seed of Israel and His blessing upon their offspring.
easy.q: What does the Lord promise to pour upon Israel’s offspring?

answers: The people will spring up and identify themselves with the Lord
The idols will begin to speak
medium.explanation: The blessing produces growth, and people declare that they belong to the Lord.
medium.q: What is expected to happen after the Lord pours out His spirit and blessing?

answers: The promise of drying the land
medium.explanation: The Lord says that He formed Jacob and will help him.
medium.q: What promise is given with the command, “Fear not, O Jacob”?

medium.explanation: The image of flourishing plants beside water represents renewal and blessing.
medium.q: What does the picture of people springing up like grass and willows communicate?

answers: Water pictures the abundance that brings God’s spirit and blessing
Water is used to make idols
challenge.explanation: Watering dry ground pictures the spiritual abundance that produces new life.
challenge.q: How are the images of water and blessing related in this passage?

answers: A turning away from the Lord
A renewed identification with the Lord and His people
challenge.explanation: The statements describe people openly identifying themselves with the Lord and Israel.
challenge.q: What is shown by the statements, “I am the Lord’s,” “by the name of Jacob,” and “by the name of Israel”?

answers: Because the Lord promises Israel help and renewal
Because the Lord commands Israel to worship idols
challenge.explanation: The Lord’s help, spirit, and blessing strengthen Israel and remove fear.
challenge.q: Why does the command, “Fear not,” fit the promise of spirit and blessing?

easy.explanation: The Lord declares, “I am the first, and I am the last.”
easy.q: How does the Lord describe Himself?

answers: There is no God beside Him
easy.explanation: He says, “beside me there is no God.”
easy.q: What does the Lord say about the existence of another God?

easy.explanation: The Lord tells Israel, “ye are even my witnesses.”
easy.q: What does the Lord call Israel?

answers: He knows and declares what is coming, while idols are useless
The idols know more than He does
There is no difference between them
medium.explanation: The Lord challenges any rival to declare future things, exposing idols as powerless.
medium.q: What distinguishes the Lord from idols in this passage?

answers: Because there is no other God to fear
Because Israel is forbidden to be a witness
medium.explanation: The Lord emphasizes that He alone is God and calls Israel to witness without fear.

answers: The Lord knows no other true God
medium.explanation: The statement emphasizes the absolute uniqueness of the Lord.
medium.q: In the phrase, “there is no God; I know not any,” what is the main point?

answers: To make an image of the Lord
challenge.explanation: Israel is called to testify that there is no God beside the Lord.
challenge.q: What role does Israel have in relation to the truth about the Lord?

answers: It emphasizes His rule over all time
It means He is made of wood
It shows that He does not know the future
challenge.explanation: Being first and last presents the Lord as sovereign over the whole course of history.
challenge.q: How does “the first” and “the last” relate to the Lord’s knowledge of history?

answers: The living, knowing Lord versus powerless idols
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the Lord’s unique knowledge and power with the emptiness of idols.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in verses 6–8?

paragraphs.title: The Futility of Idols and Their Makers

easy.explanation: The makers of graven images are said to be vanity, and their works profit nothing.
easy.q: How are the makers of graven images described?

easy.explanation: The passage describes a smith working metal and a carpenter working wood.
easy.q: What materials are used by the craftsmen in this passage?

answers: They are useful and able to speak
easy.explanation: The images cannot see, know, or profit anyone.
easy.q: What is the condition of the graven images?

answers: Their images are powerless and useless
medium.explanation: Their shame comes from laboring over objects that cannot help or save.
medium.q: Why will the makers of graven images be ashamed?

answers: The craftsman shapes the material with tools and human strength
medium.explanation: The smith and carpenter use tools, measurements, and physical labor to form the image.
medium.q: What process is described in the making of the image?

answers: He measures and shapes the wood
medium.explanation: The carpenter marks and fashions the wood according to the figure of a man.
medium.q: What does the carpenter do with a line, planes, and a compass?

answers: It shows that the image depends on human labor and is not divine
It proves that the image is alive
It shows that the craftsman does no work
challenge.explanation: The hungry and faint craftsman demonstrates that the image is merely a human product.
challenge.q: How does the craftsman’s weariness strengthen the criticism of the image?

answers: A human being makes a human-shaped image and treats it as a god
God makes the image of man
There is no connection between man and the image
challenge.explanation: The image is designed by a human craftsman in human form, yet it is worshiped as divine.
challenge.q: What contradiction is suggested by making the image “after the figure of a man”?

answers: It emphasizes that the idol is made by human hands
It proves that the image is invisible
challenge.explanation: The tools and labor expose the material, human origin of the idol.
challenge.q: Why is the detailed description of the tools important?

paragraphs.title: The Wood Used for Human Needs and for an Idol

answers: He warms himself and bakes bread
easy.explanation: He burns part of the wood to warm himself and bake bread.
easy.q: What does the man do with part of the wood?

easy.explanation: He makes the residue into a god and worships it.
easy.q: What does he make from the remainder of the wood?

easy.explanation: He says to the image, “Deliver me; for thou art my god.”
easy.q: What does the man ask the graven image to do?

answers: The same material is used for ordinary needs and for making an idol
The wood is used only for prayer
The wood is never used by people
medium.explanation: Part of the wood is burned for food and warmth, while the remainder is worshiped.
medium.q: What is the central contradiction in the use of the wood?

answers: The man fails to recognize that the image came from the same ordinary wood he burned
The man cannot see the wood
medium.explanation: He does not consider that the idol is made from common wood used for daily needs.
medium.q: Why is the worship of the image presented as blindness?

answers: He raises sheep in a field
He gathers water from a river
medium.explanation: The phrase pictures a person depending on something empty and useless.
medium.q: What does the phrase “He feedeth on ashes” suggest?

answers: He shows that it is made from wood that was also burned for fire and food
He says that it was made from heaven
He describes it as a living creature
challenge.explanation: An object made from ordinary wood used as fuel cannot possess divine power to save.
challenge.q: How does the prophet show that the idol cannot deliver?

answers: They fail to think carefully about what they have done
challenge.explanation: They do not recognize the contradiction between burning the wood and worshiping its remainder.
challenge.q: What does “They have not known nor understood” reveal about idol worshipers?

answers: A misled heart causes a person to trust in a lie that cannot save
The heart proves that the idol is alive
challenge.explanation: A deceived heart turns a person toward a false and powerless object of trust.
challenge.q: How does a “deceived heart” relate to idolatry?

answers: That he is the Lord’s servant
That he is a maker of idols
easy.explanation: The Lord reminds Israel, “thou art my servant.”
easy.q: What is Jacob and Israel told to remember?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I have blotted out…thy transgressions.”
easy.q: What does the Lord do with Israel’s transgressions?

answers: The heavens, earth, mountains, and forest
easy.explanation: All creation is called to sing and rejoice because the Lord has redeemed Jacob.
easy.q: Who is called to rejoice in Jacob’s redemption?

medium.explanation: After promising redemption, the Lord says, “return unto me.”
medium.q: What call accompanies the promise that sins are blotted out?

answers: The Lord redeems Jacob and glorifies Himself in Israel
medium.explanation: The verse says that the Lord has redeemed Jacob and glorified Himself in Israel.
medium.q: What is the connection between redeeming Jacob and Israel’s honor?

medium.explanation: Transgressions are sinful acts against the Lord’s will.
medium.q: What does “transgressions” mean in this context?

answers: It recalls Israel’s calling and special relationship with the Lord
It teaches that Israel is an idol
challenge.explanation: The servant identity recalls Israel’s covenant calling and relationship with the Lord.
challenge.q: Why is Israel’s identity as the Lord’s servant important before the promise of forgiveness?

challenge.explanation: The cloud imagery presents the Lord’s removal of sins as their disappearance from view.
challenge.q: What do the images of a thick cloud and a cloud suggest about sin?

answers: Redemption is portrayed as an event affecting the whole created world
Redemption is portrayed as a disaster
challenge.explanation: The heavens, earth, mountains, and forest are all summoned to rejoice.
challenge.q: How does creation’s rejoicing enlarge the meaning of redemption?

paragraphs.title: God’s Power and the Rebuilding of Jerusalem

easy.explanation: The Lord says that He stretched forth the heavens alone and spread abroad the earth by Himself.
easy.q: Who alone stretched out the heavens and spread abroad the earth?

answers: They will be inhabited and built
easy.explanation: The Lord declares that Jerusalem shall be inhabited and the cities of Judah shall be built.
easy.q: What will happen to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah?

easy.explanation: The Lord calls Cyrus His shepherd and says he will perform His pleasure.
easy.q: To whom does the Lord say, “He is my shepherd”?

answers: He frustrates them and turns wise men backward
medium.explanation: The Lord frustrates false signs, makes diviners mad, and turns wise men backward.
medium.q: What does the Lord do to the signs of the liars and the wisdom of diviners?

answers: He confirms His servants’ word by bringing the restoration to pass
His word has no connection with the city
medium.explanation: The Lord performs the counsel of His messengers and declares that Jerusalem will be rebuilt.
medium.q: What is the connection between the Lord’s word and the rebuilding of Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: The Lord commands the deep and its rivers to dry up, showing His power over waters.
medium.q: What does “the deep” refer to in the command, “Be dry”?

answers: He rules over the forces of nature
challenge.explanation: Commanding waters to dry demonstrates the Lord’s sovereignty over creation.
challenge.q: What does the power to dry up rivers reveal about the Lord?

answers: He is presented as the instrument through whom the Lord’s purpose will be completed
He is presented as an idol maker
challenge.explanation: Cyrus is called the Lord’s shepherd and will carry out His pleasure by rebuilding Jerusalem and laying the temple’s foundation.
challenge.q: Why is Cyrus mentioned alongside the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the temple?

answers: The Lord creates, defeats false claims, fulfills His word, and restores Jerusalem
A man makes an idol and the idol restores the city
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the Lord’s creative power to His defeat of falsehood and fulfillment of restoration.
challenge.q: What is the main progression of thought in verses 24–28?
